meta.title: Kashi — The City of Light
meta.description: Kashi — ghats, temples, Sarnath and the story of every faith. One journey from night to dawn on the Ganga.

hero.title: Kashi — older than history itself
hero.titleSecondary: काशी — जो इतिहास से भी पुरानी है
hero.subtitle: A single lamp is lit in the dark. The ghats wake. The Ganga keeps flowing, the way it has for longer than anyone remembers.

common.englishNote: Some details are shown in English.

day.title: A day in Kashi
day.intro: In a single day the city is born three times: at dawn on the river, at noon in the lanes, and at dusk in the flame of the aarti.
day.hint: Scroll to move through the day

dawn.title: Subah-e-Banaras
dawn.caption: The sun rises from the far bank. A conch sounds, the boats push off, and the steps slowly fill.

noon.title: Noon in the galis
noon.caption: The smell of kachori, the flash of brass, silk threads on a loom, and a small shrine at every turn.

dusk.title: Ganga Aarti
dusk.caption: Seven tiered lamps rise together. Bells, conch, smoke, and the whole ghat catches like a single flame.

places.title: Places of Kashi
places.intro: Ghats, temples, stupas, mosques, gurudwaras, churches and the maths of the saints, all in one city. Filter them, find them on the map, and read each one's story.

faiths.title: One Kashi, every faith
faiths.intro: The city belongs to no one tradition. Each has its own morning here, and all share one river. Below, in order of arrival, each with equal room.
faiths.order: In order of arrival in Kashi

hindu.name: Hindu
hindu.essence: Shiva's own city, where even death is release.
hindu.translation: To die in Kashi is liberation.

jain.name: Jain
jain.translation: Souls render service to one another.

buddhist.name: Buddhist
buddhist.essence: Sarnath, where the Buddha first taught.

islamic.name: Islamic
islamic.essence: The weavers' lanes, a shared Ganga-Jamuni culture, minarets above the river.
islamic.translation: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

bhakti.name: Bhakti saints
bhakti.essence: Kabir, Ravidas, Tulsidas: voices larger than temple or mosque.
bhakti.translation: Where do you search for me, friend? I am right beside you.

sikh.name: Sikh
sikh.essence: The sangat of Guru Nanak and Guru Tegh Bahadur at Nichibagh.
sikh.translation: One Creator, whose name is Truth.

christian.name: Christian
christian.essence: A two-hundred-year-old church in the Cantonment, and the city's schools and hospitals.
christian.translation: I am the light of the world.

projects.title: Projects & the new Kashi
projects.intro: Beside the old city a new one is being built. Every status here was checked against a source; anything that could not be confirmed is listed as announced.
projects.unverified: Not confirmed by an official source

festivals.title: A year of festivals
festivals.intro: Kashi's calendar runs on the moon. Every month some flame is lit: on a ghat, in a temple, or across the river.
festivals.lunarNote: Dates follow the lunar calendar and shift every year; check before you travel.

food.title: The taste of Banaras
food.intro: Food here is eaten standing, from a clay cup or a leaf plate, and it changes from dawn to midnight.

itineraries.title: Itineraries
itineraries.intro: One day, two or three: every plan starts before sunrise and ends at the aarti.
itineraries.placesNote: Named places are described in the Places section

practical.title: Practical
practical.intro: Getting here, when to come, and how to behave on the ghats and in the temples.

air.title: By air
air.text: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport (Babatpur) is 25 km north-west of the city, with direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Kolkata and Hyderabad; a prepaid taxi to the ghats takes about an hour.

rail.title: By rail
rail.text: Varanasi Junction (Cantt) is the main station; Banaras (Manduadih) and Kashi stations also serve the city. The Vande Bharat from Delhi takes about 8 hours; Cantt to Godowlia is 20–30 minutes by auto.

road.title: By road
road.text: On NH-19 (Delhi–Kolkata) and NH-31; Lucknow is 300 km, Prayagraj 120 km. Cars cannot enter the old-city lanes: from Godowlia it is on foot or by cycle-rickshaw.

season.title: Best season
season.text: October to March: cool mornings, clear skies, Dev Deepawali and Shivratri. April–June climbs past 40 °C; in July–September the Ganga rises, many ghats go under water and boat services can stop.

etiquette.title: Etiquette
items: Leave shoes, leather and phones outside temples; keep shoulders and knees covered.
Do not photograph cremations at Manikarnika or Harishchandra Ghat; watch from a distance and in silence.
At the aarti, do not stand in front of the priests' platforms; watch from the steps or a boat.
Agree boat and guide prices before you start; avoid touts offering 'special darshan'.
Nothing plastic goes into the Ganga; buy only clay diyas.
Cover your head in a gurudwara, stay outside a mosque at prayer times, keep quiet during a church service.

finale.title: The Ganga Aarti
finale.text: Every evening, as the sun goes down behind the city, the lamps are raised at Dashashwamedh. The journey that began with one diya ends here, with a thousand.
finale.closing: ॐ नमः शिवाय · Har Har Gange
finale.closingSecondary: Come to Kashi. The lamps are lit.
